title: When the Archive Breaks Revisited
premise: Emrys Galloway investigates 'impossible accidents'—deaths that shouldn't have happened aboard ships that never flew. When her own mother's name appears on the manifest of the Meridian, a colony vessel lost forty years ago, Emrys follows a trail of forged records to a hidden archive where the last cryosleep bays of humanity are being quietly triaged: half will wake, half will be left in the dark, and someone has been editing history to hide who decided. The impossible accidents were murders—eliminations of anyone who found the selection list. In the end, Emrys broadcasts the full manifest and the names of the deciders on Earth's final transmission loop, choosing truth over mercy: everyone wakes or no one does, and she accepts exile as the price of having made herself visible.
about_author: Isandro Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years reconciling cargo manifests for vessels that sank under disputed circumstances. They write from a houseboat off the Azores and refuse to confirm whether any of their novels are memoir.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Between relay stations, Emrys works an insurance claim for a reactor death aboard a ship whose flight logs don't exist. She notices the same forged certification stamp on three unrelated cases. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; the reader learns she has spent years making herself administratively invisible.

chapters.title: A Name That Should Be Ash
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Cross-checking archives, she finds her mother—declared dead forty years ago—listed as a passenger on the Meridian, a ship that never flew. Her hands shake; the record is dated after the official loss date. Emotional beat: grief reopened as suspicion; invisibility was supposed to protect her from exactly this.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She bribes a records clerk on Ceres Station for the original manifest microfilm and finds it surgically altered—her mother's entry overwritten over another name. Someone wanted her to find this, or wanted no one to. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Adjuster's Creed
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, flashback interleave. We learn how she became an investigator of impossible accidents: her mother vanished on the Meridian's 'maiden' voyage, and the settlement check came with a confidentiality clause Emrys never signed. Emotional beat: inheritance of silence; she realizes her whole career was a search disguised as work.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident Number Nine
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A witness to the manifest forgery dies in a decompression 'accident' hours before their meeting. The kill signature matches her three earlier cases. Emotional beat: cold fear—the pattern isn't coincidence; it's a cleanup crew, and she may be next on the list.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Following shipping routes backward, she reaches a derelict orbital yard and discovers the Archive: thousands of intact cryopods, the real survivors of the evacuation fleets, held in secret while Earth's surface died. Only half the bays are powered. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at the scale of the lie.

chapters.title: The Selection List
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Inside the Archive's control spine she finds the triage ledger—who wakes, who stays frozen—and her mother's name is not on either column. It's on a third list: objections filed, then struck through. Emotional beat: fury; her mother didn't die by accident, she died by committee.

chapters.title: Custodian
chapters.summary: POV Sefu Okonkwo, the Archive's aging custodian. He reveals he inherited the selection protocol from his predecessors and has kept it running out of duty, not belief. He warns Emrys that the 'deciders' still live, awake, among the last habitats. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between guilt and justice.

chapters.title: What the Loop Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Earth's final transmission loop—a decades-old broadcast repeating humanity's last messages—is scheduled to end when its power cell fails. Sefu shows her the loop can carry one final payload. Emotional beat: dawning realization that the dead have one channel left, and she holds the key.

chapters.title: The Deciders
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She infiltrates a habitat council session and sees them: nine officials who signed the triage order, now respectable elders administering the waking schedule like a benevolent lottery. One of them recognizes her surname. Emotional beat: dread and disgust; evil wearing administrative competence.

chapters.title: Offered a Bay
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The deciders offer her a place on the wake list—and her mother's pod restored—in exchange for the stolen ledger and her silence. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare; the price of survival offered to her personally, echoing the theme.

chapters.title: Refusal, Notarized
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She declines and escapes the habitat with a copy of the ledger, but Sefu is detained as collateral. Her escape burns every alias she has built. Emotional beat: the cost of visibility begins—she can never be anonymous again, and someone else is paying for it.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Never-Flew
chapters.summary: POV Sefu, in detention. Interrogated by the deciders' security chief, he stalls by reciting passenger names aloud, turning the roster into a litany they cannot bear to hear. Emotional beat: quiet defiance; memory as resistance.

chapters.title: Allies Among the Frozen
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She contacts families of the strike-through list scattered across the relays—people who also received impossible settlements. Some refuse to help; three agree. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity; justice outside the law requires volunteers, not institutions.

chapters.title: Sabotage Ethics
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Planning the broadcast, the allies argue: hijacking the transmission loop could doom the Archive's power grid and kill everyone still frozen. Emrys must design a plan that wakes the pods before the loop dies. Emotional beat: moral weight of engineering; every option costs lives.

chapters.title: The Waking Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. She discovers the thaw sequence can be triggered remotely but takes eleven hours—exactly the window before security traces her signal. The chapter is a ticking-clock technical siege as she threads the uplink through relay stations. Emotional beat: focused terror; competence as prayer.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Relay Seven
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. One ally sells the plan to buy his own family's bay. Security converges; two allies are captured; Emrys barely escapes with the uplink half-complete. Emotional beat: betrayal's bitter arithmetic—the price of survival paid in other people.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Hiding in the Archive itself, she plays the recovered objection recording: her mother arguing before the council that selective waking is murder, her voice steady then breaking. Emotional beat: catharsis; Emrys stops investigating her mother and starts inheriting her.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: POV Emrys and Sefu alternating. Climax begins: Emrys triggers the waking protocol and loads the full manifest, the triage ledger, and the deciders' names onto Earth's final transmission loop. Alarms flood the Archive. Emotional beat: irreversible commitment; the point of no return crossed with open eyes.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief vignettes. Across the system, cryopods open—thousands of people waking to a transmission naming their saviors and their jailers. The deciders' habitats erupt in reckoning; some are arrested by their own security, others flee. Emotional beat: chaotic, imperfect justice arriving all at once.

chapters.title: The Price Itemized
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Standing trial by the newly woken community—not for the broadcast but for the deaths her plan's chaos caused—she pleads guilty to the cost and not the cause. Sefu testifies for her; the sentence is exile from the Archive. Emotional beat: sober resolution; justice outside the law must still answer to the living.

chapters.title: Revisited
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, epilogue. Exiled on the long route again, now visibly named on every manifest, she receives a message from a woman who woke from pod 4471: her mother's friend, carrying a letter her mother wrote for whoever finished what she started. Emrys reads it, sets course, and signs her own name to the log. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted; survival finally worth its price.
